source_text.body:
Protect family time and log commitments with an always-on agent
A Microsoft executive told his Scout agent to protect family dinnertime and log every promise made to him and by him; it once sent a poorly formatted run-on email.
Done with
MS
Microsoft Scout
What they did
Omar Shahine, a Microsoft Corporate Vice President, uses Scout, an always-on agent inside Teams that reads messages, email and calendars. He set a goal for it to protect family dinnertime. He also asked it to log every promise made to him and every commitment he has made. His agent is nicknamed Sebastian.
How it went
The source gives no measured results. Shahine admits the agent once sent an email that was one big run-on sentence with no formatting. He advises choosing carefully which tasks to automate and which still need direct supervision.
Worth knowing
Access is limited: Copilot Frontier subscribers get a desktop app now, and enterprise access opens via waitlist from Q4 2026. Prompt injection is a known risk, so supervise tasks that matter.
Try it yourself
with
Microsoft Scout
Copy prompt
Act as my always-on assistant. Protect [time block, e.g. 6-8pm weekday dinner] by declining or flagging any meeting invites that overlap it, and log every commitment I make or that others make to me from my email and calendar into a running list with [who, what, due date]. Before sending any email or declining any invite on my behalf, show me the draft and wait for my approval, and keep the formatting short and clean.
Original source: https://businesschief.com/technology-and-ai/microsoft-announces-scout-an-always-on-ai-agent-for-teams
